data.content_ref: inline:The target's central category-error argument is self-undermining: its own counterconditions concede within-evaluation evidence that can distinguish genuine reliability from mere compliance (boundary-error signatures, process traces, controlled distribution shifts). Having conceded these, it cannot coherently maintain that the distinction 'is not a property of the single evaluation at all.' More importantly, it never engages the problem's core ask: argue for or against the claim that a panel of trained non-experts following an explicit checklist will, on average, produce more reliable judgments than a single domain expert relying on intuition. By restricting its entire argument to the separability sub-question and declaring that sub-question a category error, it produces no stance on the primary claim—no weighing of panel reliability versus expert intuition—leaving the first half of the problem unaddressed.
